subject: math
title: Grade 4 Fractions
seo_title: Grade 4 Fractions Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Represent fractions from halves to tenths using drawings, tools, and standard fractional notation, and explain the meanings of the denominator and the numerator
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on fractions for the Ontario curriculum: numerator and denominator, fractions of shapes and sets, comparing fractions, counting past 1 with mixed numbers, and 3 × 1/4. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The denominator tells how many equal parts make the whole. The numerator tells how many parts you count.
key_sub: A bigger denominator means smaller parts, so 1/8 < 1/4. Count by fourths past 1: 3/4, 1, 1 1/4. And 3 × 1/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.
body_html:
Numerator and denominator

A fraction names equal parts of a whole. The denominator (bottom number) tells how many equal parts make the whole. The numerator (top number) tells how many of those parts you are counting.

Halves, thirds, fourths, fifths, sixths, eighths and tenths: the name comes from the denominator.

Fractions of a set

The whole can be a set of objects. The denominator is the number of objects in the set.

Example

A bag has 5 red marbles and 3 blue marbles. What fraction are blue?

The whole set is 5 + 3 = 8 marbles. 3 are blue.

Answer: 38

Compare and order

Same denominator: the parts are the same size, so more parts is more. 58 > 38.

Same numerator: you have the same number of parts, so look at their size. A bigger denominator means smaller parts.

Example

3 pizzas are shared by 4 friends. 3 pizzas are shared by 5 friends. Which share is bigger?

Each friend gets 34 or 35. Fewer sharers means bigger shares.

Answer: 34 > 35

Count by fractions past 1

Count by fourths: 14, 24, 34, 1, 1 14, 1 24. After 4 fourths, you have 1 whole. A whole number and a fraction together, like 1 14, is a mixed number.

Adding the same unit fraction

Adding the same unit fraction again and again is multiplication.

Example

Owen runs 14 km, 5 times. How far does he run?

5 × 14 = 54. 4 fourths make 1 km, and 1 fourth is left.

Answer: 1 14 km

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking 18 is bigger than 14 because 8 is bigger than 4A bigger denominator means smaller parts, so 18 < 14
Mixing up the numbers: writing 43 for 3 of 4 equal partsParts counted on top, parts in the whole on the bottom: 34
Calling unequal parts “thirds” or “fourths”Fractions need equal parts
In a set of 5 red and 3 blue, writing 35 for blueUse the whole set: 38
3 × 14 = 312Only the number of parts changes: 34
Writing 54 as 1 154 fourths make 1, and 1 fourth is left: 1 14

faq.q: What fractions do Grade 4 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum, Grade 4 students work with fractions from halves to tenths. They name fractions of shapes and sets, compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator, count by fractions past 1 (like 5/4 = 1 1/4) and see that 3 × 1/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4.

faq.q: What is the difference between the numerator and the denominator?
faq.a: The denominator (bottom number) tells how many equal parts make the whole. The numerator (top number) tells how many of those parts you are counting, so 3/4 means 3 of 4 equal parts.
Cut the same pizza into 4 pieces and into 8 pieces. With fewer pieces each piece is bigger, so 1/4 is bigger than 1/8, even though 8 is a bigger number.

faq.q: How do you explain 3 × 1/4 to a Grade 4 student?
faq.a: 3 × 1/4 means 3 groups of 1/4, or 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4. That is 3 fourths, 3/4; the denominator stays 4 because the pieces are still fourths.

items.q: The circle is cut into 4 equal parts. What is each part called?
items.e: 4 equal parts are called fourths. Each part is one fourth, 14. Four fourths make the whole shape.

items.q: How do you say 310 in words?
items.e: Read the numerator first, then the name of the parts. 310 is three tenths: three of the ten equal parts.

items.q: How do you say 58 in words?
items.e: Read the numerator first, then the name of the parts. 58 is five eighths: five of the eight equal parts.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 3 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 3. 2 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 2. The answer is 23.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 5 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 5. 2 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 2. The answer is 25.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 4 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 4. 3 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 3. The answer is 34.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 6 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 6. 5 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 5. The answer is 56.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 10. 7 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 7. The answer is 710.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.e: The circle has 8 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 8. 3 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 3. The answer is 38.

items.q: In 38, what does the denominator 8 tell you?
items.e: The denominator is the bottom number. In 38 it tells you the whole is cut into 8 equal parts (eighths).

items.q: In 56, what does the numerator 5 tell you?
c: Each part is 15.
items.e: The numerator is the top number. In 56 it tells you 5 of the 6 equal parts are counted.

items.q: What is the denominator of 46?
items.e: The denominator is the bottom number. In 46 the denominator is 6.

items.q: What is the numerator of 710?
items.e: The numerator is the top number. In 710 the numerator is 7.

items.q: Which fraction has a numerator of 2 and a denominator of 5?
items.e: The numerator (top) is 2 and the denominator (bottom) is 5, so the fraction is 25.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is not shaded?
items.e: The bar has 6 equal parts, so the denominator is 6. 1 part is shaded, so 6 − 1 = 5 parts are not shaded. The answer is 56.

items.q: What fraction of the circle is not shaded?
items.e: The circle has 5 equal parts, so the denominator is 5. 3 parts are shaded, so 5 − 3 = 2 parts are not shaded. The answer is 25.

items.q: Which picture shows 34 shaded?
items.e: 34 needs 4 equal parts with 3 shaded. That is picture D. A has 4 parts, but they are not equal. B shows 14. C has 5 parts, so it shows 35.

items.q: Which picture shows 25 shaded?
items.e: 25 needs 5 equal parts with 2 shaded. That is picture A. B shows 35. C has 5 parts, but they are not equal. D has 7 parts, so it shows 27.

items.q: Leah says 13 of this bar is shaded. Is she right?
c: No. The parts are not equal.
Yes. Each part is a third.
No. It shows 23.
items.e: No. The 3 parts are not equal. Thirds must be 3 equal parts. The shaded part is bigger than the others. It is really 12 of the bar.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 1 whole?
items.e: 66 means 6 of the 6 equal parts, so the whole thing is counted. 66 = 1 whole.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 10 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 10. 4 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 4. The answer is 410. The shaded parts do not need to be side by side.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 8 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 8. 6 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 6. The answer is 68. The shaded parts do not need to be side by side.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: The whole is the set of 6 counters, so the denominator is 6. 2 are green: 26. Do not compare green with white (2 to 4).

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: The whole is the set of 8 counters, so the denominator is 8. 3 are green: 38. Do not compare green with white (3 to 5).

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: The whole is the set of 10 counters, so the denominator is 10. 4 are green: 410. Do not compare green with white (4 to 6).

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: The whole is the set of 5 counters, so the denominator is 5. 3 are green: 35. Do not compare green with white (3 to 2).

items.q: What fraction of the counters are not green?
items.e: There are 8 counters in the set. 5 are green, so 8 − 5 = 3 are not green. The answer is 38.

items.q: What fraction of the balls are big?
items.e: In a set, each object is one part, even if it is bigger. There are 4 balls and 1 is big: 14.

items.q: A bag has 5 red marbles and 3 blue marbles. What fraction of the marbles are blue?
items.e: The whole set is 5 + 3 = 8 marbles. 3 are blue, so 38 are blue. 35 compares blue with red; it does not use the whole set.

items.q: A box has 10 pencil crayons. 3 of them are broken. What fraction of the pencil crayons are broken?
items.e: There are 10 pencil crayons in the set and 3 are broken. So 310 are broken.

items.q: 4 friends go skating. 3 of them wear mitts. What fraction of the friends wear mitts?
items.e: The set is the 4 friends, so the denominator is 4. 3 wear mitts: 34.

items.q: A box has 6 muffins. 5 are blueberry and the rest are bran. What fraction of the muffins are bran?
items.e: 6 − 5 = 1 muffin is bran. 1 out of 6 muffins: 16.

items.q: Maya has 8 hockey cards. 3 of them are goalie cards. What fraction of her cards are not goalie cards?
items.e: 8 − 3 = 5 cards are not goalie cards. 5 out of 8 cards: 58.

items.q: How many more parts must be shaded to show 78?
items.e: To show 78, 7 parts must be shaded. 3 are shaded now, so shade 7 − 3 = 4 more.

items.q: How many more parts must be shaded to show 910?
items.e: To show 910, 9 parts must be shaded. 4 are shaded now, so shade 9 − 4 = 5 more.

items.q: In which set are 35 of the counters green?
items.e: 35 of a set means 5 counters in all with 3 green. That is set D. A has 8 counters, so it shows 38. B shows 25 green. C has 8 counters, so it shows 58.

items.q: In which set are 26 of the counters green?
items.e: 26 of a set means 6 counters in all with 2 green. That is set C. A shows 46 green. B has 8 counters, so it shows 28. D has 4 counters, so it shows 24.

items.q: These 3 counters are 13 of a set. How many counters are in the whole set?
items.e: 13 means the set has 3 equal groups, and this is 1 group. 3 groups of 3 is 3 × 3 = 9 counters.

items.q: These 4 counters are 12 of a set. How many counters are in the whole set?
items.e: 12 means the set has 2 equal groups, and this is 1 group. 2 groups of 4 is 2 × 4 = 8 counters.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: All 5 counters are green. 5 out of 5 is 55, which is 1 whole set.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which fraction is greater?
items.e: Same denominator, so the parts are the same size. Compare the numerators: more parts is more. 58 > 38.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which fraction is greater?
items.e: Same numerator, so you have the same number of parts. A smaller denominator means bigger parts. 23 > 25.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which fraction is greater?
items.e: Same numerator, so you have the same number of parts. A smaller denominator means bigger parts. 34 > 310.

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: All the numerators are 3, so look at the denominators. The smallest denominator (4) gives the biggest parts. 34 is the greatest.

items.q: Which fraction is the least?
items.e: All the denominators are 8, so the parts are the same size. The smallest numerator is the least: 28.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 13, 110, 15
c: 13, 15, 110
110, 15, 13
15, 13, 110
13, 110, 15
items.e: Same numerator. The biggest denominator is the smallest fraction, so start with 110. Least to greatest: 110, 15, 13.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 24, 28, 26
c: 24, 28, 26
26, 28, 24
28, 26, 24
24, 26, 28
items.e: Same numerator, 2. Eighths are smaller than sixths, and sixths are smaller than fourths. Least to greatest: 28, 26, 24.

items.q: Order from greatest to least: 410, 910, 610
c: 610, 910, 410
910, 610, 410
410, 610, 910
910, 410, 610
items.e: Same denominator, so compare the numerators: 9 > 6 > 4. Greatest to least: 910, 610, 410.

items.q: Group A: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 4 friends. Group B: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 5 friends. In which group does each friend get more pizza?
items.e: Group A: each friend gets 34 of a pizza. Group B: each gets 35. Same numerator, and fewer sharers means bigger shares, so 34 > 35. Group A gets more.

items.q: Group A: 6 friends share 5 subs equally. Group B: 6 friends share 4 subs equally. In which group does each friend get more?
items.e: Group A: each friend gets 56 of a sub. Group B: each gets 46. Same denominator, so compare numerators: 56 > 46. Group A gets more.

items.q: 2 granola bars are shared equally by 3 friends. How much does each friend get?
items.e: Cut each bar into thirds. Each friend gets 1 third from each of the 2 bars: 23 of a bar. The number of sharers is the denominator.

items.q: Which share is bigger: 2 pancakes shared by 3 friends, or 2 pancakes shared by 8 friends?
items.e: Shared by 3: 23 of a pancake each. Shared by 8: 28 each. Same numerator, so the smaller denominator is bigger: 23 > 28.

410 > 45
items.e: Check each one. With the same numerator, a bigger denominator means a smaller fraction. 45 > 410 is true, because fifths are bigger than tenths.

items.e: With the same denominator, the parts are the same size, so the fraction with more parts is greater. 710 > 310 is true.

items.q: Arjun says 18 is greater than 14 because 8 is greater than 4. Is he right?
c: No. 14 is greater.
items.e: A whole cut into 8 parts has smaller parts than a whole cut into 4 parts. So 14 > 18.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. How much is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 4 equal parts. 5 fourths are shaded, which is 54. 4 fourths make 1 whole, and 1 more fourth is 14. So 54 = 1 14.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. How much is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 2 equal parts. 5 halves are shaded, which is 52. 2 halves make 1 whole, and 1 more half is 12. So 52 = 2 12.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. How much is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 4 equal parts. 7 fourths are shaded, which is 74. 4 fourths make 1 whole, and 3 more fourths is 34. So 74 = 1 34.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. How much is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 10 equal parts. 13 tenths are shaded, which is 1310. 10 tenths make 1 whole, and 3 more tenths is 310. So 1310 = 1 310.

items.q:
Count by fourths. What comes next?
34, 1, 1 14, ?
items.e: Add 14 each time. 1 14 + 14 = 1 24.

items.q:
Count by halves. What comes next?
3, 3 12, ?
items.e: Add 12 each time. 3 12 + 12 = 4, because 2 halves make 1 whole.

items.q:
Count by thirds. What comes next?
1 13, 1 23, ?
items.e: Add 13 each time. 1 23 + 13 = 1 33, which is 2. 3 thirds make a whole.

items.q:
Count by tenths. What comes next?
2 810, 2 910, ?
items.e: Add 110 each time. 2 910 + 110 = 2 1010, which is 3.

items.q:
Count by tenths. What number is missing?
9 710, ?, 9 910, 10
items.e: Count by tenths: 9 710, 9 810, 9 910, 10. Each step adds 110.

items.q: How many fourths make 2 wholes?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole. 2 wholes need 4 + 4 = 8 fourths, so 84 = 2.

items.q: You count by halves from 0 to 10. How many halves do you count?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. 10 wholes need 10 × 2 = 20 halves.

items.q: Which fraction is more than 1 whole?
items.e: A fraction is more than 1 when the numerator is greater than the denominator. 43 is 4 thirds, and 3 thirds make 1, so 43 is more than 1. 33 is exactly 1.

items.q: 54 = ?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole. 54 is 5 fourths: that is 1 whole (4 fourths) and 1 fourth left over. So 54 = 1 14.

items.q: 72 = ?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. 72 is 7 halves: that is 3 wholes (6 halves) and 1 half left over. So 72 = 3 12.

items.q: 73 = ?
items.e: 3 thirds make 1 whole. 73 is 7 thirds: that is 2 wholes (6 thirds) and 1 third left over. So 73 = 2 13.

items.q: 1310 = ?
items.e: 10 tenths make 1 whole. 1310 is 13 tenths: that is 1 whole (10 tenths) and 3 tenths left over. So 1310 = 1 310.

items.q: 1 34 = ?
items.e: Each whole is 4 fourths. 1 whole = 4 fourths. Add 3 more: 4 + 3 = 7. So 1 34 = 74.

items.q: 2 12 = ?
items.e: Each whole is 2 halves. 2 wholes = 4 halves. Add 1 more: 4 + 1 = 5. So 2 12 = 52.

items.q: Count by fourths. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Each whole has 4 equal spaces, so each space is 14. The dot is 7 spaces from 0: that is 74 = 1 34.

items.q: Count by thirds. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Each whole has 3 equal spaces, so each space is 13. The dot is 8 spaces from 0: that is 83 = 2 23.

items.q: Which multiplication is the same as 14 + 14 + 14?
items.e: 14 + 14 + 14 is 14 added 3 times. That is 3 groups of 14: 3 × 14.

items.q: 3 × 14 = ?
items.e: 3 × 14 means 14 + 14 + 14. Three fourths is 34. The parts are still fourths, so the denominator stays 4.

items.q: 5 × 18 = ?
items.e: 5 × 18 means 5 copies of 18: 5 eighths, or 58. Do not multiply the denominator.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 4 × 110?
c: 110 + 110 + 110 + 110 + 110
110 + 110 + 110 + 110
110 + 110 + 110
items.e: 4 × 110 means add 110 4 times: 110 + 110 + 110 + 110 = 410.

items.q: 6 × 14 = ?
items.e: 6 × 14 is 6 fourths, 64. 4 fourths make 1 whole, and 2 fourths are left. So it is 1 24.

items.q: 7 × 13 = ?
items.e: 7 × 13 is 7 thirds, 73. 6 thirds make 2 wholes, and 1 third is left. So it is 2 13.

items.q: ? × 15 = 45
items.e: 45 is 4 fifths, so you need 4 copies of 15: 4 × 15 = 45.

items.q: Hana skates 14 of a lap around the rink, 3 times. How much of a lap does she skate in all?
items.e: 3 × 14 = 14 + 14 + 14 = 34 of a lap.

items.q: A hockey game has 3 periods of the same length. Ethan watches 2 periods. What fraction of the game does he watch?
items.e: The game has 3 equal parts, so the denominator is 3. He watches 2 of them: 23.

items.q: A tourtière is cut into 8 equal pieces. The family eats 5 pieces. What fraction of the tourtière do they eat?
items.e: There are 8 equal pieces, so the denominator is 8. They eat 5 pieces: 58.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. Chloe’s family eats 4 slices. What fraction of the pizza is left?
items.e: 6 − 4 = 2 slices are left out of 6 equal slices. That is 26 of the pizza.

items.q: A ringette team has 10 players. 7 wear blue helmets and the rest wear white helmets. What fraction of the players wear white helmets?
items.e: 10 − 7 = 3 players wear white helmets. 3 out of 10 players: 310.

items.q: Mei uses 13 cup of flour for each batch of maple cookies. She makes 5 batches. How much flour does she use?
items.e: 5 × 13 = 53 cups. 3 thirds make 1 cup, and 2 thirds are left: 1 23 cups.

items.q: Each lap of the school field is 14 km. Owen runs 5 laps in the Terry Fox Run. How far does he run?
items.e: 5 × 14 = 54 km. 4 fourths make 1 km, and 1 fourth is left: 1 14 km.

items.q: Noah drinks 3 bottles of water on a canoe trip. Each bottle holds 12 L. How much water does he drink?
items.e: 3 × 12 = 32 L. 2 halves make 1 L, and 1 half is left: 1 12 L.

items.q: Kai has granola bars cut into fourths. He eats 5 fourths. How many granola bars does he eat?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole bar. 5 fourths is 1 whole bar and 14 more: 1 14 bars.

items.q: Zoe says 3 × 15 = 315. Is she right?
c: No. It is 35.

items.e: 3 × 15 means 15 + 15 + 15. The parts stay fifths, so the answer is 35. Only the number of parts changes.

items.q: Arjun ran 310 km. Sofia ran 34 km. Who ran farther?
items.e: Same numerator, 3. Fourths are bigger than tenths, so 34 > 310. Sofia ran farther.

items.q: Ava’s group of 4 shares 3 subs equally. Liam’s group of 4 shares 2 subs equally. In which group does each person get more?
items.e: Ava’s group: 34 of a sub each. Liam’s group: 24 each. Same denominator, and 3 > 2, so Ava’s group gets more.

items.q: A sugar bush worker fills 110 of a barrel with sap each hour. How much of a barrel is filled after 12 hours?
items.e: 12 × 110 = 1210. 10 tenths make 1 barrel, and 2 tenths are left: 1 210 barrels.
